storyTitle: Implement validation rules ensuring mandatory cosmetic classification fields (category, application type) are populated before persistence

functional.title: Successfully save cosmetic classification with both mandatory fields populated
preconditions: User is logged in with a role that has permission to create/edit cosmetic classifications
User is on the cosmetic classification form page
The system has predefined category and application type dropdown options available
No unsaved changes exist on the form

steps.action: Select a valid category from the 'Category' dropdown field (e.g., 'Skin Care')
steps.expectedResult: The 'Category' dropdown displays the selected value 'Skin Care' and no validation error is shown

steps.action: Select a valid application type from the 'Application Type' dropdown field (e.g., 'Leave-on')
steps.expectedResult: The 'Application Type' dropdown displays the selected value 'Leave-on' and no validation error is shown

steps.action: Fill in any other required fields on the form with valid data
steps.expectedResult: All fields accept the entered data without errors

steps.action: Click the 'Save' button to persist the cosmetic classification record
steps.expectedResult: The record is saved successfully. A success message such as 'Cosmetic classification saved successfully' is displayed. No validation errors appear.

steps.action: Navigate to the saved record or refresh the page to verify persistence
steps.expectedResult: The saved record displays 'Skin Care' as the category and 'Leave-on' as the application type, confirming data was persisted correctly

postconditions: The cosmetic classification record is persisted in the database with category = 'Skin Care' and application type = 'Leave-on'
User remains on the confirmation or detail page of the saved record
An audit trail entry is created for the new record creation

functional.title: Validation error displayed when attempting to save without selecting category
preconditions: User is logged in with permission to create cosmetic classifications
User is on the cosmetic classification form page
The 'Category' field is empty/not selected
The 'Application Type' field has a valid selection

steps.action: Leave the 'Category' dropdown field unselected (default empty/placeholder state)
steps.expectedResult: The 'Category' field shows its default placeholder text (e.g., 'Select Category')

steps.action: Select a valid application type from the 'Application Type' dropdown (e.g., 'Rinse-off')
steps.expectedResult: The 'Application Type' field displays 'Rinse-off'

steps.action: Click the 'Save' button to attempt persistence
steps.expectedResult: The save operation is blocked. A validation error message is displayed near the 'Category' field stating 'Category is required' or similar mandatory field message

steps.action: Observe the form state and UI indicators
steps.expectedResult: The 'Category' field is highlighted in red or with an error indicator. The form remains in edit mode. No data is persisted to the database.

postconditions: No record is saved to the database
User remains on the cosmetic classification form page with the validation error visible
The 'Application Type' selection is retained so user does not lose their input

functional.title: Server-side validation prevents persistence even if client-side validation is bypassed
preconditions: User is logged in with permission to create cosmetic classifications
User has access to browser developer tools
The cosmetic classification API endpoint is known

steps.action: Open browser developer tools and navigate to the Console or Network tab
steps.expectedResult: Developer tools are open and ready

steps.action: Craft a direct API request (e.g., via fetch or curl) to the cosmetic classification save endpoint with an empty 'category' field and a valid 'application type'
steps.expectedResult: The API request is sent to the server

steps.action: Observe the API response
steps.expectedResult: The server returns an HTTP 400 (Bad Request) or 422 (Unprocessable Entity) response with a validation error message indicating 'Category is required'

steps.action: Craft another API request with a valid 'category' but empty 'application type'
steps.expectedResult: The server returns an HTTP 400 or 422 response with a validation error message indicating 'Application Type is required'

steps.action: Verify no records were created in the database
steps.expectedResult: No new cosmetic classification records exist in the database from these requests

postconditions: Server-side validation prevents any record from being persisted without mandatory fields
Appropriate HTTP error codes and messages are returned
Database integrity is maintained
